video_title: Solana’s President on the Next Era of Crypto | with Lily Liu at Breakpoint 2026 in London
transcript: Welcome to Real Vision at Solana Breakpoint 2026 in London. I'm Arto Rashinski and I'm joined by Lily Louu, president of the Salena Foundation. Thank you so much for joining us. >> Thanks for having me. >> So, we're having this conversation as the conference is kicking off. Everything is about to go into full gear. Um, so that's for context for people watching afterwards. This is the sixth edition of of Breakpoint. Uh, and it's my second. It feels different in the sense of we are in London. We've hit the mainstream, but what do you want to highlight this year in particular? Uh, at Breakpoint, does the location play into it? >> Uh, sure. So I think last year is when people started to really hear us talk about internet capital markets. I think that's always been the purpose of blockchain which is that this is financial infrastructure for the internet. Uh and so there's kind of an order of operations of how you go build an ecosystem. Obviously if there's no blockchain there's no reason to be doing anything else because that's kind of like that's the the core infrastructure that's core technology. So you got to ship that first. Uh and then uh for a number of years what you really had to build next is uh build a community of principally developers using map blockchain building applications building businesses uh and actually wanting to come to your ecosystem because it's a place where they can actually build business and you know put very simply somewhere where they feel like they can make money right and that's something that I think we've been always very upfront about which is that uh we're building an economy we're not just building a blockchain we're just building a network we're building not even just a community. We're here to build an economy. Uh and all of those things are contributors to the economy. And that I think that in this order of operations, there's building a network. There's building community developers and applications. And then the next thing uh because this is about finance after all is building uh uh is bring assets on chain. Uh and over the last couple of years, uh I think it's become pretty top of mind. Topization, real world assets, bring trady on chain. And there's various ways that people have talked about it uh over really actually the last 10 years. It used to be securization. Now we call it tokization. Okay, great. But what it's really about is on the internet uh you can actually have native financial rails uh for all assets and all ways that people want to use those assets. And so the simplest way that happens is stable coins and payments. Uh and the most sort of uh the most advanced way that typically happens is high frequency trading of assets, right? uh and there's a number of things in between there uh where increasingly you're bringing on RWA assets um as collateral for collateral markets and when borrow and so you see this uh you see this real explosion of uh of innovation around uh around what you can do with finance when it's native to the internet you can issue assets um you have full composibility of those assets uh and uh and and the introduction of uh payments adjacent to trading adjacent projection mark codes adjacent to lend to borrow and all of that being natively available within any wallet right any wallet any mobile app any internet uh any internet interface >> so looking at the agenda it seems to me that we now have more speakers associated with traditional finance >> older institutions uh obviously there's masterard there's western union there's barlays many many such institutions it feels less like a cryptonative conference. So, what does that tell us in terms of how Breakpoint has changed over the years? >> You know, we've been asked a number of times over the last few months, how would you describe Breakpoint? And uh I love how our team has uh has summed that up. It's like Comic Con meets Milkin. [laughter] And if you just walk the floor outside, I think it really does feel like that. Uh and another that surprised us a little bit is as we were putting the program together for Breakpoint, we had such such a tremendous amount of interest from uh from traditional companies um so payments companies from Wall Street uh and folks that are uh very active in either the payment side of things um or the tokenization side of things um or the trading side of things. And so uh so I think that um blockchain really has grown up and I think even as Salana uh I think you know blockchain is starting to kind of blend into everything else because finance is a part of everything else right finance is not its own sort of island out there. Um it is how you do capital formation for innovation. Capital formation for uh for uh for good and services. And so finance has never stood on an island itself. Um it's how markets come together and it's markets in goods and services. It's markets in innovation. It's markets in you know creating creating something new for the future. Um and so I think that uh that's what we've seen in this kind of evolution over the last six break points as well. Um at one point in time we were so heavily focused on startups and builders and founders and developers and that's always the core part of our community. Uh but over the last few years as we've continued to develop as Salana as an ecosystem and as an economy uh then we've gotten to sort of uh move into the next level to bring on asset issuers um to be used in those apps to be used on the network which is Salana. >> Breakpoint um it's been a very exciting time for for Salana. Uh Breakpoint always is um you've had some really big announcements leading up to Breakpoint uh and at Breakpoint itself. So could you walk us through some of the the big ones like the DTCC announcement or the Samsung partnership uh because it really feels like a watershed moment for Salana. >> Absolutely. Uh so Samsung we announced that about a month ago uh and that's actually now live uh with Samsung wallet in the United States. That's 82 million wallets that are using USDC built natively into the wallet. So that's tremendously exciting uh because when you think about you know this this thesis that people have talked about for a long time which is that if you have internet native finance then you can integrate finance into anywhere and everything and all the places that people use the internet which is on mobile on your computer 5 and a half billion people globally right and uh and that's a bigger market than anything else that we've seen scale exponentially on the internet because if you look at all the mobile apps and web and two-sided marketplaces you name uh social media, all of these huge trends that um have just really exploded and changed uh changed really everything um over the last 30 years. They're all sort of uh growing within a language market which is max that are one and a half billion native English speakers in the world and there's also one and a half billion native Chinese speakers in the world. Uh and that's basically been you know if you want to put it in sort of the more commercial terms or a little bit more commercial cycle the market right now the total addressable market uh is one and a half billion and we've seen just how uh incredible the innovation has been around even just to serving that market. Uh well, you've got five and a half billion people on the internet and uh and what they have in common is not necessarily a language, but the fact that all of those five and a half billion people use money. >> Could just be payments. Uh it could be uh it could be more than that. Could be investments, investments, savings, lending, borrowing, uh participating in uh in a financial market in some way or some form at some point at some point in time. uh and I think that's really been the mission that we as Salana and also this industry as blockchain more broadly has always been after. Uh so Samsung has been a real watershed movement for us. Uh the announcement rentCC uh super excited about uh you know obviously uh they are the bedrock of uh US capital markets which is uh by and large you know for sure the most important capital market in the world and the dominant one. When you talk about finance, it's just the reality that every dollar uh that either moves through a payment or moves through investments pretty much runs through the US financial system. Uh and so for the DTCC uh to be integrating Sana in 2027 is uh very meaningful, very meaningful step. Uh but then that's also part of a lot of the work we've been doing on equities and tokenizing equities for about a year and a half now. Um and as Salana, we've always taken the perspective that we want to provide infrastructure that meets users wherever they are. Uh and so from a year and a half ago with the launch of Xdocs, um uh we were uh the key partner on that one with Kraken and with Payword and XDocs. Um and every time there's been a new model around tokenized equities, we've always wanted to be there. Uh and so DTCC certainly is a real capstone of that. Uh but then also if you look across trans the transfer agent tokenization model if you look across RFQ different models brokerage models um and SPV models every time there's been some sort of innovation in how you bring tokenized assets on chain we thought you know we want to be there and we want you we'll let the standards you know figure it out in the market which one is going to become the standard um but whatever that might be it's going to be on salon. How do those conversations go? Because Samsung is is a forwardthinking company, but I'm guessing DTCC is a bit more of a traditional entity. So, how do you how did that all come together? Because yes, we um people in crypto know of its advantages, but how do you start those conversations with institutions like DTC to say you this is what you guys been doing for decades, we can improve it. How do you convince them? >> Well, first of all, I uh I not surprisingly I think our team is incredible uh in leading uh and you know spending years on these conversations. Um and so Nick who leads institutional for us uh he's been uh he's been uh building that relationship and having those conversations for years with DTCC, not just DTCC, all of the other uh tokenization models across equities and across other asset classes. And then Lou uh who who leads APAC has been working for years uh with Samsung as well and our team more broadly has been working with Samsung for years on various different uh thinking about various ways to potentially work together. Uh but ultimately uh ultimately what a a firm like Samsung uh or a firm like the DTCC ultimately what's going to convince them is that it's good for them to do this uh and that this is a product meaning Salana as a network and Salana as a community as an ecosystem um is something that's going to help them uh grow their business. Uh and so ultimately the market no one is bigger than the market. Uh and uh and in finance the most important thing to everybody is to be a part of the largest market and to be a part of the most liquid market. And I think one of the core insights that we had at Salana from early on is that uh people would trade off practically everything else in order to be a part of the largest market. And so that's I think been the core part of our thesis as to why public blockchains should exist, will exist and are going to eventually be the home of the largest capital market uh which is the the internet capital market. Uh because that is uh that is in eventually the largest aggregation of liquidity and of capital that can possibly exist. Um and people are going to want to be a part of that market. And I think that that is also something uh that we've seen in in a shift over the last 10 years where uh I understand why a number of institutions have for a long time felt more comfortable with a permissioned private environment. Uh but then ultimately the reason why people actually are interested in tokenization and and in blockchain is ultimately because they can reach an audience they could not reach before. And the only way you're going to go reach that audience you could not reach before is is if you're stepping outside of the geographic bounds of current infrastructure infrastructure which is definitionally geographically bounded. Uh and everyone wants to re reach net new distribution. Uh and I think that's one of the reasons why you've seen this unsafeable shift which is still continuing and I believe accelerating um where folks actually are interested in being on a public blockchain because there's net new users liquidity uh and that's where uh that's where uh the the largest market may emerge. >> So let's expand on that problem solving aspect of it. Um we have heard the the motto of institutions are coming for years institutions are here. We've heard about tokenization real world assets. Let's expand on on the problem solving aspect. Explain to us why we should care that this trend of tokenization is uh is happening. What is the the real world problems that it is solving? >> Sure. And I think it comes down to distribution. And so if we just look at equities for example as an asset class. Um if you get if you dig into uh which equities actually get distribution and look uh start to look into the financial plumbing behind this. The theory that markets are all efficient because there's no transaction costs and information uh is uh is perfectly uh is perfectly distributed to all market actors. Obviously is not how markets actually work. and has never been the way markets have worked. uh and so when you look at for example asset allocation at scale uh and how much is driven by passive versus active uh I believe in the US market depending on you count on how you count it's you know upwards of 60% which is passively allocated and then if you look at what is uh how that passive allocation actually gets allocated to how many names on which benchmark in which markets uh then what it does is uh uh you want to be in for in the indust indic ies of whether it's the S&P 500, Fortune 100, so on and so forth that have that lock in that attract assets into those components, right? Into those index constituents. What that means is if you're not in the 100, if you're not in the 500, then you're not on the conveyor belt, you're not on an escalator. Uh and that means that your dollar of cash flow is not actually being fully valued in the same way. Not because the quality of your business is not is necessarily less, but it's just because you're not on the escalator and there's only 100 spots on that escalator or 500 spots on the escalator. And uh and so when it comes when you talk about sort of capital allocation and where whether capital is actually flowing to the most deserving assets and the most deserving teams, uh uh the theory of fully efficient markets is not actually true. And so I think the beneficiaries of uh of things that uh uh that that are going to be very interesting on on blockchain and the internet um are like so many other friends in tech. It's about opening up uh mid and longtail markets and matching those. Right? That's what you saw with for example riders and drivers on Uber. There's always been demand for uh a ride and then also a driver. a rider and a driver at any given point in time in some location at a certain time. But there was no way to discover and clear that market until you had this new technology platform which is the mobile phone which could follow you to any location at any given point of time when you would have that demand for uh for a rider or a driver and uh and so I think that the internet sort of has always been uh matching mid and longtail demand which does not mean it's lowquality demand or lowquality assets. It just means that these are undiscovered uh underdiscovered um assets and investment opportunities and uh and that's the type of thing that you can only solve with new technology and that's why we keep on talking about internet capital markets. >> So at previous breakpoint you said that Solena is positioning itself as the financial infrastructure for the 5.5 billion users of the internet. So where do you think Solana is uh compared to its competitors? Where do you see your biggest advantages? Uh, and where maybe you're lagging slightly? How would you compare Salana to the rest of the crypto markets right now? >> Um, I think that I think we do something quite different than uh what what there's a diversity of things that people have articulated within blockchain and what the blockchain infrastructure is for. Uh I remember when I first got into this industry about 12 years ago, there was already this raging debate as to at that point it was really just Bitcoin, but is Bitcoin a store of value or is it a technology platform? So I think for a long time there's always been this debate as to uh what is a blockchain, what is it for? And is it more technology or is it more finance? Meaning it's obviously both, right? It's technology and it's being used for financial stuff. Um but then uh there's been these different thesis on is it a technology platform superpowered by finance. That's for example the web 3 thesis of read write own right it's a technology platform decentralized backend for all sorts of different applications that has finance built into it and then there's the vision of this is financial infrastructure that is being superpowered by technology. Uh this is uh this is where you can put finance on chain and make it programmable through technology. And that might seem like six and a half a dozen where oh is it a tech platform powered by finance or is a finance platform powered by technology but actually to me that is upstream of everything you see in the differences between ecosystems. Uh and I think that uh because we as Salana have taken this view of this is finance first superpowered by technology that is upstream of the choices you make around your architecture. So for example, no sharding uh because you need to protect everyone else to be part of the largest market and so therefore you've got to have unified liquidity and try to never ever give that up right because everyone else will give up practically everything in order to be a part of that largest market over the long term. So that view of its finance powered by technology is something that you see in the core architectural choices of the Salami ecosystem. I think that that is also reflected in the way we think about community and the way we think about the ecosystem which is that this is uh economic infrastructure for people to go build a business and for people to innovate and be and and to successfully innovate. Of course, big part of that is economic success, right? And so we've always embraced uh building a uh successful economy and helping people uh make money and uh we sometimes even refer to Salana uh going forward being this API for capitalism, API for finance, API for capitalism. Uh and so I think that that kind of philosophy and that culture is also uh is also you know perhaps different um because we're finance first before we are technology. Have you had to do any trade-offs along the way to to get there? >> I think there's there's always trade-offs. Uh there's trade-offs in everything. Um but then, you know, you have to you have to choose your constraints in order to you you hope you make the right trade-offs, but then you always choose your constraints. Um and then uh and then you choose how to flourish within that. And so I think one of the constraints you could say from the very early days is that you're just going to be a single shard. Um and uh just or so we're only ever about mainet. Uh and uh and I think that you see that um people have called that focused before. Um but it's kind of like it's a built-in focus where we don't have 100 different uh 100 different teams building SVM. If you're building SVM, it's Sana. If you're building a Sana, it's SVM. And then you got to focus on all the other things um that are really hard about you know building a company, building a startup and building an audience, building community, right? Um and so I think that that focus has gotten built in and that's one area where we just chose a constraint. Uh and uh and that also allowed to build this community to build a network effect around that. Um and I think uh some other differences as we go forward is uh just continued clarity that this is financial infrastructure. You know in this industry that was debated for a long time uh and uh and looking backwards I think it's very easy to even articulate now to folks who are part of the ICO era part of NFTTS part of gaming that well really all of those things are financed too. They were markets being built around whatever that asset was at the time. ICO is essentially capital formation onchain for cryptonative projects. you know clearly not many of them are still around but that was you know like a v 0.1 uh experimentation in that direction which I think will continue to come back and again again it's fundamentally this is about capital formation for innovation uh and then I think with NFT and NFTs in gaming um uh the sort of tech before finance view saw that as creator economy saw that as like a new form of social web three social >> meme coins as well right >> uh sure but then you know for NFTs in gaming. The way I saw that is with NFTTS, it was creating a market around JPEGs. And this this technology is so powerful uh and its ability to bring people together um that you could actually create markets around JEX and harness that interest. Uh yes, it's a lot of speculative energy, but be able to harness that interest and that energy and create very meaningful markets around it. Uh and then with gaming uh I think that was actually one place where you saw the starkkest kind of comparison between a tech versus a financed driven view of the world where the the techdriven view was oh now you can run your games uh the back end of your games entirely on chain. But there was never really any answer as to why you'd actually want to do that. Does that help you build a better game? Is that a better experience for your users? Uh is it less expensive or why would you want to do that? Uh and then the the finance uh the finance-driven view of the world on blockchain gaming would be to say well uh if you can integrate payments rails uh stable coins uh or integrate uh markets infrastructure around in-game items then that gives you the ability to add a new aspect of gameplay uh and also potentially and broadens your to the user base. But that to me has always been around uh around the way financial infrastructure uh creates a better experience and also expands a market. >> Uh and so I think that gaming is actually a really good example of how the tech versus financed driven view of the world led people to very different uh in in very different directions when it came to the intersection of blockchain and gaming. >> Somehow miraculously we've avoided the topic of AI for the most part. So, how has the rise of AI affected Salana and um how has it affected the road map for for Salana? >> Um well, I think that uh blockchain is always front and center especially in blockchain is DeFi and DeFi is blockchain. Uh so we're absolutely front and center when it comes to and not just as a salonist, our our industry is front and center when it comes to security. I think that's going to it's going to be a pretty tough next 18 months for really everybody and uh and blockchain within that. Um as we look at security incidents that are going to be hitting financial infrastructure, transportation infrastructure, you name it, uh we're certainly not going to be left out of that as blockchain. In fact, we may even be and I think you already seen that uh we're blockchain industry is pretty front and center on that. So we're going to be security hardened first. uh but it is um I think one of the one of the things that it forces us to do as an industry is um as an industry we've been so focused around uh around you know move fast and break things um ship quickly and then iterate that whole culture that I think dominates a lot of the tech world um and it's about you know not missing the innovation whereas the culture that I think has driven a lot of technology and startups always has been um you uh you don't you don't want to be the person that missed the cure that could have saved a million people. >> So you're going to care you're going to optimize around that type of risk rather than the risk of you're the doctor report patient, right? Type one versus type two error. >> And I think this is now a time where we might have to reorient for the next year or two and really get security right. Otherwise, the things that you build on top of that um are in the age of AI is is going to be uh it's just a different risk calculation. It's just a different risk function these days than it was even six months ago. >> This is a very exciting time uh for us at break point. This been a very exciting time for founders, developers uh in crypto and yet sentiment is just the wider sentiment is quite poor especially with the price action once again. What is your message to people who are feeling burnt out and almost ready to give up on crypto? Because they hear all those fantastic headlines how institutions are coming, how everything is improving and they don't see that reflected in in price action. So, how do you reconcile this? >> Look, the the price action that affects us all is price action that comes that looks at all of blockchain as an asset class first and foremost. And so so asset allocation goes into there's risk assets and then there's sort of frontier technology within that and then uh blockchain every you know number of years becomes the top of the pile and it rotates to the bottom of the pile. And so clearly what happened over the last couple of years is all of that risk and innovationoriented capital went into AI. >> And so this is this is not because there is not forward activity happening within blockchain. Um but this is uh just this is allocation to the asset class. Uh and about one year ago there was a tremendous amount of energy and attention into DATs. And like happens every so often within blockchain, um there's over exuberance and then an overcorrection of that. Uh and what we've also seen in 2026 is if you remember the week before the SpaceX IPO, we were basically at a similar at a similar place in terms of price action. And uh and then one week before the Antropic IPO, we happened to be almost exactly in the same place when it comes to price action. And uh and none of those uh monthtomonth, week to week, quartertoquarter um uh charts are because of the fundamentals of this industry. Really none of them. Now on the flip side, that can also be true when you're on the other side of the market with the overexuberance. Um but quite literally I believe what's happening right now uh uh in this specific sort of weak time frame is uh people are uh are liberating cash in order to fund their uh their allocation request for the anthropic IPO and that's all coming out of risk capital. Where is risk capital coming out of? It's coming out of so people may be monetizing their SpaceX position. They're monetizing Bitcoin uh and they're pulling money out of other tech things and more sort of frontier tech things and the biggest pile that comes out of is blockchain. >> So before we wrap I have a few rapid fire questions. One word to describe Salana >> uh Breakpoint [laughter] >> AI um crypto friend or foe >> friend. The best part of Breakpoint, >> I think just uh being a part of the community and bringing the community together. It's pretty awesome. >> Salana only or a multi-chain future? >> Uh Salana primarily. >> Okay, thank you so much, Le. >> Thank you. >> Thank you so much. >> Thanks. >> So, you obviously like this video enough that you've got to the end. That's quite a big task, but listen, do me a favor. Hit the like and subscribe button and also check out what video's next cuz I think you'll love it. But if you want even more, and when I'm talking more, I'm talking about memberergenerated ideas, incredible alpha research, everything there to help you in your journey, just head to realton.com/join for the best financial intelligence out there and the pure alpha that's within the platform.
